title: Attenuated cast reduction and lane-aware kernel chooser for mixed-precision paths
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our mixed-precision serving paths (INT8 and FP8 variants) incur per-request overhead from transient casts and headwise divergence in kernel choice. In production traces we see dequant/cast overheads dominating small-request latency tails and causing inefficient kernel warmups for interleaved prefill/decode workloads. Goal: implement a lane-aware kernel chooser that reduces ephemeral cast churn (attenuated cast reduction) and stabilizes kernel selection across short-lived microbatches to improve median and tail latency without regression to sample quality. This ticket tracks the design, prototypes, perf validation, and rollout plan for a conservative implementation that can be enabled via a runtime flag and gated by telemetry.

Why now: Increasing Dedicated and Private usage by customers with latency-sensitive chat features has exposed amplification of cast overhead when serving short prefill-heavy requests. Previous efforts reduced bulk token throughput cost but did not sufficiently address the per-request casting penalty and kernel thrashing in multi-tenant setups.

Scope:
- Implement lane-aware chooser that groups logical heads/token-lane patterns observed in the first N tokens and pins kernel flavor (INT8/FP8/FP16) and cast strategy for the remainder of a request.
- Introduce attenuated cast reduction: coalesce ephemeral casts into batched, amortized operations during prefill to avoid repeated tiny tensor conversions.
- Add lightweight heuristics to fall back early if quantized path introduces quality regression beyond threshold.
- Instrument telemetry and build a canary rollout.

Non-goals: global rewrites of kernel fusion, new quantized kernel implementations, or changing model weights/quantization params in this ticket.

Technical approach:
1) Signal extraction: sample key metrics from the first 1-4 tokens (head usage distribution, attention sparsity estimate, sequence-length hint) to score compatibility with quantized kernels.
2) Lane-aware chooser: a compact scorer that selects a kernel flavor and cast policy per-request. It will prefer INT8 fastpath when the score indicates stable attention patterns and memory layout compatibility.
3) Attenuated cast reduction: instead of doing ephemeral cast for every attention block, accumulate per-layer casting ops during prefill stage and execute a single coalesced cast/transpose before decode. Use zero-copy views where supported.
4) Safety checks: run a lightweight per-request quality comparator that hashes and compares logits for a small set of probe prompts in the canary stage to detect regression.
5) Telemetry: capture counters for chooser decisions, cast reductions, per-token latency delta, and quality probe mismatch rate.

Acceptance criteria: [list]
- Median per-request prefill latency reduced by at least 8% on representative INT8 workloads (A100 p4d baseline).
- 99th percentile tail latency not increased.
- Token throughput on long-sequence decode workloads remains within 2% of baseline.
- No more than 0.5% requests show quality probe mismatches in canary.
- Runtime flag and config exposed so we can enable per-customer.

Implementation plan (work items): [list]
- Prototype chooser in the runtime sandbox with config knobs and unit tests.
- Implement attenuated cast aggregator in the attention prefill path with CI tests for correctness.
- Add lightweight quality comparator harness and microbench suite.
- Run cluster-level A/B on dedicated pool for 48h with telemetry gates.
- Rollout gradual enablement by customer tier with automatic rollback on telemetry breach.

Telemetry and dashboards: [list]
- chooser.decisions.{int8,fp8,fp16} (counter)
- cast_reduction.coalesced_ops (gauge)
- latency.prefill.median and latency.prefill.p99 (histogram)
- quality.probe.mismatch_rate (rate)
- kernel_thrash.rate (counter for kernel switches within request)

Benchmarks to run: [list]
- microbench: 1-4 token prefill + single-token decode (50k samples).
- chat-sim: 8-turn chat with mixed short and long messages (10k sessions).
- long-decode stress: 2048 token generation steady-state throughput.

Risks and mitigation: [list]
- Risk: Attenuated casts could hide per-layer incompatibilities leading to silent quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative scoring threshold, early fallback to safe FP16, and quality probes in canary.
- Risk: Coalescing casts may increase peak memory transient pressure. Mitigation: limit coalescing window size and fall back to incremental casts if OOM risk detected.
- Risk: Kernel pinning may reduce multiplexing efficiency for multi-tenant nodes. Mitigation: enable pinning only for requests exceeding a cost threshold and provide opt-out via customer config.

Link to artifacts and PRs: [list]
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/runtime/attenuated-cast-chooser
- Proto PR (sandbox): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/quant/attenuated-cast-canary

Dependencies: [list]
- Existing quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) and their kernel metadata service (ENG-ids referenced in runtime catalog).
- Telemetry infra for per-request histograms.

Next steps and timeline: [list]
- 2026-03-12: complete prototype and unit tests.
- 2026-03-15: land attenuated casting path behind flag and run microbench cluster canary.
- 2026-03-22: 48h A/B on dedicated pool, evaluate telemetry.
- 2026-03-29: staged rollout to select customers if gates pass.
